title: How to spend your time more wisely, with Cassie Holmes, PhD

sentences.en: Do you ever feel like there aren't enough hours in the day for you to do the things you want to do?
sentences.zh: 你是否曾觉得一天里的时间总是不够用，无法完成你想做的事？

sentences.en: Pressed by endless work and family obligations, have you ever dreamed of quitting this life and moving to a remote beach where you could read, paint, play music, or just veg?
sentences.zh: 在无休止的工作和家庭责任的压力下，你是否曾梦想过辞去这种生活，搬到一个偏远的沙滩上，在那里读书、画画、玩音乐，或者纯粹发呆？

sentences.en: When we feel time poor, endless hours to do whatever we please sounds like the ultimate luxury.
sentences.zh: 当我们感到时间匮乏时，有源源不断的时间去做任何我们高兴的事听起来就像是终极的奢侈。

sentences.en: But research suggests that the relationship between leisure time and contentment is not so straightforward and that it's not the amount of time that you have
sentences.zh: 但研究表明，闲暇时间与满意度之间的关系并非如此简单，决定你幸福感的

sentences.en: but how you spend it that determines your happiness.
sentences.zh: 不是你拥有多少时间，而是你如何使用这些时间。

sentences.en: So is there an ideal amount of free time?
sentences.zh: 那么，是否存在一个理想的自由时间量呢？

sentences.en: Is it possible to have too much free time or too little?
sentences.zh: 自由时间是太多好，还是太少好？

sentences.en: Who's happier?
sentences.zh: 谁更幸福？

sentences.en: People who focus on the value of time or those who focus on the value of money?
sentences.zh: 是那些关注时间价值的人，还是关注金钱价值的人？

sentences.en: And are there ways to increase your sense of time affluence without making a major change like quitting your job?
sentences.zh: 有没有什么方法可以在不做出辞职这样重大改变的情况下，增加你的时间富裕感？

sentences.en: Is it possible to make time-sucking chores like housework and commuting seem less onerous?
sentences.zh: 有没有可能让诸如家务和通勤这样吞噬时间的琐事看起来不那么繁重？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学对话》，这是美国心理学会的主打播客，旨在探讨心理学科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Cassie Holmes, a professor of marketing and behavioral decision-making at UCLA's Anderson School of Management.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是加州大学洛杉矶分校安德森管理学院的市场营销与行为决策教授卡西·霍姆斯博士。

sentences.en: She studies time and happiness, including such questions as how focusing on time or money affects happiness and how the meaning of happiness changes over one's lifetime.
sentences.zh: 她研究时间和幸福感，包括关注时间或金钱如何影响幸福感，以及幸福感的含义在一生中如何变化等问题。

sentences.en: Her research has been published in top psychology journals and covered by media outlets including the New York Times, the Wall Street Journal, and National Public Radio.
sentences.zh: 她的研究发表在顶尖的心理学期刊上，并被《纽约时报》、《华尔街日报》和全国公共广播电台等媒体报道。

sentences.en: Her new book is called Happier Hour,
sentences.zh: 她的新书名为《更快乐的一小时》，

sentences.en: How to Beat Distraction, Expand Your Time, and Focus on What Matters MoSt.
sentences.zh: 如何战胜分心、拓展时间并专注于最重要的事情。

sentences.en: It aims to provide a research-based, practical guide on how to think about time and how to spend your time to live a happier life.
sentences.zh: 它旨在提供一本基于研究的实用指南，指导如何看待时间和如何度过时间以过上更幸福的生活。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining me today, Dr. Holmes.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你今天能来，霍姆斯博士。

sentences.en: Hi, Kim.
sentences.zh: 嗨，金。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我。

sentences.en: It's a treat to be here.
sentences.zh: 能来到这里真是一种享受。

sentences.en: You study time poverty and time affluence.
sentences.zh: 你研究时间贫困和时间富裕。

sentences.en: What do those terms mean?
sentences.zh: 这些术语是什么意思？

sentences.en: What makes somebody time poor or time affluent?
sentences.zh: 是什么让一个人感到时间贫困或时间富裕？

sentences.en: Is it just the amount of leisure time that you have?
sentences.zh: 仅仅是你拥有的闲暇时间的多少吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so time poverty is defined as the acute feeling of having too much to do and not enough time to do it.
sentences.zh: 是的，时间贫困被定义为一种强烈的感受，即有太多事要做，而没有足够的时间去完成。

sentences.en: And it is a negative experience and it has negative consequences.
sentences.zh: 这是一种负面体验，会带来负面后果。

sentences.en: And it's also a very pervasive experience.
sentences.zh: 而且这是一种非常普遍的体验。

sentences.en: In a national poll that I just conducted, we found that nearly half of Americans report feeling time poor.
sentences.zh: 在我刚刚进行的一项全国性民意调查中，我们发现近一半的美国人报告说他们感到时间贫困。

sentences.en: Women tend to feel more time poor than men.
sentences.zh: 女性往往比男性感到更多的时间贫困。

sentences.en: Folks who are working tend to feel particularly impoverished.
sentences.zh: 工作的人往往会感到特别匮乏。

sentences.en: And folks who are working who have a partner who works with young kids are perhaps the most time poor.
sentences.zh: 而那些既要工作、有育儿伴侣还要照顾年幼孩子的上班族，可能感受到的时间贫困最为严重。

sentences.en: But it's not just being a parent or working.
sentences.zh: 但这不仅仅是因为为人父母或工作。

sentences.en: Individuals who do not work and individuals who don't have kids are also subject to feeling time poor.
sentences.zh: 不工作的人和没有孩子的人同样会感到时间贫困。

sentences.en: The effects of it are negative.
sentences.zh: 它的影响是负面的。

sentences.en: And so I will, in a second, get to our research that looks at the overall relationship between the amount of discretionary time people have and their happiness.
sentences.zh: 因此，我一会儿会讲到我们的研究，该研究着眼于人们拥有的可支配时间量与他们的幸福感之间的整体关系。

sentences.en: But pulling from across studies, including some of my own, looking at what are the effects of being time poor, research shows that it makes people less healthy
sentences.zh: 但结合各项研究（包括我自己的部分研究）来看时间贫困的影响，研究表明它会让人变得不那么健康，

sentences.en: because they're less likely to spend their time exercising.
sentences.zh: 因为他们不太可能花时间去锻炼。

sentences.en: It makes them also less healthy because they're more likely to eat fast food that is readily available and not necessarily healthy.
sentences.zh: 它也让人变得不那么健康，因为他们更有可能吃现成且未必健康的快餐。

sentences.en: People delay going to the doctors.
sentences.zh: 人们会拖延去看医生的时间。

sentences.en: It also makes us feel or be less kind.
sentences.zh: 它还让我们感觉不到或表现得不够善良。

sentences.en: So in some of my work, we found that when people don't feel like they have a lot of time, they become very stingy with their time, less likely to spend time to help others.
sentences.zh: 因此，在我的某些研究中，我们发现当人们觉得时间不够用时，他们在时间上会变得非常吝啬，不太可能花时间去帮助别人。

sentences.en: We also have some work showing that when people feel time poor, they become less confident in being able to achieve their goals.
sentences.zh: 我们还有一些研究表明，当人们感到时间贫困时，他们对自己实现目标的能力会变得缺乏信心。

sentences.en: And now the question is, what about the emotional ramifications?
sentences.zh: 现在的问题是，情感上的后果呢？

sentences.en: And this research was actually motivated by a personal experience as someone who falls into all of those demographic categories
sentences.zh: 这项研究其实是由一次个人经历激发出来的，作为一个符合所有这些人口统计学特征的人，

sentences.en: of being someone who works with young kids, with a partner who works.
sentences.zh: 即带着年幼的孩子工作，且伴侣也在工作。

sentences.en: I felt and feel particularly time poor.
sentences.zh: 我曾经并且现在依然感到特别的时间贫困。

sentences.en: And it led me to be like, oh my gosh, should I go ahead and quit my job?
sentences.zh: 这让我忍不住想，哦天哪，我是不是该直接辞职算了？

sentences.en: I can't really sort of keep up at this pace.
sentences.zh: 我实在无法以这种节奏坚持下去了。

sentences.en: But that begged the question is, would I feel happier if I had a whole lot more hours in my day to spend how I wanted?
sentences.zh: 但这就引出了一个问题：如果我一天中能有大把的时间来随心所欲地度过，我会不会感到更幸福？

sentences.en: So hours to spend on discretionary activities.
sentences.zh: 也就是用来从事可支配活动的时间。

sentences.en: So to answer that question, I recruited a couple of my favorite collaborators,
sentences.zh: 为了回答这个问题，我招募了几位我最喜欢的合作者，

sentences.en: Hal Hirshfield and Marissa Sharif.
sentences.zh: 哈尔·赫什菲尔德和玛丽莎·谢里夫。

sentences.en: And we looked at the relationship between the amount of hours you have within your regular day to day life to spend on discretionary activities.
sentences.zh: 我们研究了你在日常生活中花在可支配活动上的时间与幸福感之间的关系。

sentences.en: So discretionary activities being those things that you want to spend your time on.
sentences.zh: 可支配活动就是那些你想花时间去从事的事情。

sentences.en: That includes relaxing, sort of passive leisure, like watching TV, taking naps.
sentences.zh: 这包括放松，比如看电视、小睡等被动休闲。

sentences.en: It also includes active leisure, like playing sports, going and watching sporting events.
sentences.zh: 它还包括积极的休闲，比如进行体育运动、观看体育比赛。

sentences.en: And it includes hobbies as well as social connections, so spending time with friends and family.
sentences.zh: 它包括爱好以及社交联系，比如与朋友和家人共度时光。

sentences.en: And we looked at what's the relationship between that and life satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 我们研究了这与生活满意度之间的关系。

sentences.en: We looked at a couple of data sets to analyze this.
sentences.zh: 我们研究了几个数据集来对此进行分析。

sentences.en: And I think the most sort of telling, because it's the biggest data set and most broadly representative of folks in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我认为最具说明意义的是美国时间使用调查数据，因为它是最大的数据集，最能广泛代表美国民众。

sentences.en: is the American Time Use Survey data.
sentences.zh: （重复或语气词省略或平顺处理，见下文）

sentences.en: And that data includes tens of thousands of working and non-working Americans.
sentences.zh: 该数据集包含成千上万名工作和不工作的美国人。

sentences.en: And what it does is it captures a regular day and assesses how does each individual spend that day?
sentences.zh: 它的作用是记录常规的一天，并评估每个人是如何度过那一天的？

sentences.en: What activities are they spending their day doing?
sentences.zh: 他们把一天都花在做什么活动上了？

sentences.en: And what we did is for each individual, we calculated how much time that day they spent on discretionary activities, like those that I just mentioned.
sentences.zh: 我们所做的是，为每个人计算出他们在当天花在可支配活动上的时间有多少，就像我刚才提到那些一样。

sentences.en: And by the way, you might be wondering, well, like, how did you come identify those as discretionary activities?
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，你可能在想，好吧，你们是怎么把这些确定为可支配活动的？

sentences.en: And for that, we actually went to a different sample of participants, presented them with the whole list of 138 different activities,
sentences.zh: 为此，我们实际上采访了另一组参与者，向他们展示了包含138种不同活动的完整清单，

sentences.en: activity categories, and asked them, is this discretionary?
sentences.zh: 活动类别，并问他们，这具备可支配性吗？

sentences.en: By discretionary means something you want to do, or that feels worthwhile in its own right.
sentences.zh: 所谓可支配，意味着你想做的事，或者其本身就让你觉得很有价值的事。

sentences.en: And we pre-registered that we would count any activity.
sentences.zh: 我们预先注册了我们将计算任何活动。

sentences.en: It was a very conservative test that any activity that more than 90% of participants identified as discretionary, we would count those.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常保守的测试，任何被超过90%的参与者认为是可支配的活动，我们都会计算在内。

sentences.en: We also had a more lenient threshold with any activity that more than 75% viewed as discretionary.
sentences.zh: 我们还有一个更宽容的门槛，即任何被超过75%的人视为可支配的活动。

sentences.en: The pattern holds regardless of that particular threshold.
sentences.zh: 无论采用哪个特定的门槛，这种规律都成立。

sentences.en: So we calculated for each individual how many hours in that regular day that they spend on discretionary activities, and we related it to life satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们计算了每个人在常规一天中花在可支配活动上的时间有多少小时，并将其与生活满意度联系起来。

sentences.en: What we found was interesting.
sentences.zh: 我们发现的结果很有趣。

sentences.en: The pattern of results showed an upside down U shape.
sentences.zh: 结果呈现出倒U形曲线。

sentences.en: So that's to say that when you have very little time, you see low happiness.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，当你时间非常少时，你会发现幸福感很低。

sentences.en: Yes, that is me.
sentences.zh: 是的，那就是我。

sentences.en: That is those of you who also feel time poor.
sentences.zh: 也就是你们这些也感到时间贫困的人。

sentences.en: And in this particular data set, it suggested that two hours in the day on discretionary activities counts as too little time.
sentences.zh: 在这个特定的数据集中，它表明一天中花在可支配活动上的时间为两小时，算作时间太少。

sentences.en: But what was also interesting was the other end of the spectrum, where we also saw that it dipped down in terms of happiness or life satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 但同样有趣的是频谱的另一端，我们也看到幸福感或生活满意度出现了下降。

sentences.en: And what we found was that beyond about five hours of discretionary time, people were also less happy.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，当可支配时间超过大约五个小时后，人们的幸福感反而会降低。

sentences.en: And so between two and five hours, the relationship was quite flat.
sentences.zh: 因此，在两到五个小时之间，这种关系相当平缓。

sentences.en: And so what that is suggesting is that except at the extremes, it's not so much about the amount
sentences.zh: 这表明，除了极端情况之外，问题与其说是你拥有的时间数量，

sentences.en: of time you have, then the question comes in, how are you spending the hours that you have?
sentences.zh: 不如说是你如何利用你所拥有的时间？

sentences.en: But I think going back to sort of the opening motivation for this is, you know,
sentences.zh: 但我觉得回到最初促成这项研究的动因，你知道的，

sentences.en: would I, and I'm using me as an example because as representative of so many who are feel time poor,
sentences.zh: 我（我以自己为例，因为我代表了那么多感到时间贫困的人），

sentences.en: would I actually feel happier if I were to quit my job and have a whole lot more free time?
sentences.zh: 如果我辞职并拥有大量空闲时间，我真的会感觉更幸福吗？

sentences.en: And the answer, according to our set of studies is no.
sentences.zh: 而根据我们的一系列研究，答案是否定的。

sentences.en: So people don't feel productive then if they have that much free time is what you found that
sentences.zh: 所以你发现，如果人们有那么多的空闲时间，就会觉得自己没有生产力，

sentences.en: they feel like they've been wasting their days and therefore in some sense, wasting their lives.
sentences.zh: 他们会觉得自己一直在浪费日子，因此在某种意义上是在浪费生命。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So getting into the reason for that pattern of results.
sentences.zh: 因此，让我们来探讨这种结果模式背后的原因。

sentences.en: So what we found was with too little time, it is feelings of stress.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，当时间太少时，带来的是压力感。

sentences.en: People feel higher levels of stress and that is associated with less satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 人们感受到更高水平的压力，这与较低的满意度相关。

sentences.en: For the too much time, we did find that people felt less productive.
sentences.zh: 对于时间太多的情况，我们确实发现人们觉得自己生产力降低了。

sentences.en: They felt like a lacking sense of purpose within their days.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得日常生活中缺乏一种目标感。

sentences.en: And this is picking up on other research that shows that we do have a drive to be somewhat productive.
sentences.zh: 这呼应了其他研究，这些研究表明我们确实有一种追求一定生产力的驱动力。

sentences.en: And being busy communicates not only to others, but also to ourselves that we have accomplished something.
sentences.zh: 保持忙碌不仅向他人，也向我们自己传达了我们已经完成了一些事情的信息。

sentences.en: And so having day in and day out of having so many hours available just to spend relaxing, you see this dip in satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 因此，日复一日地拥有大把可供挥霍和放松的时间，你会发现满意度出现了下降。

sentences.en: What is also interesting, we see that it's not just about sort of discretionary time per se,
sentences.zh: 同样有趣的是，我们发现这不仅仅关乎可支配时间本身，

sentences.en: because there are some discretionary activities that do feel productive and do feel worthwhile.
sentences.zh: 因为有些可支配活动确实让人觉得很有生产力，也很有价值。

sentences.en: And we analyzed the amount of time that individuals spent within the discretionary activities on those that they viewed as productive and worthwhile.
sentences.zh: 我们分析了个人在可支配活动中花在那些他们认为有生产力和有价值的事情上的时间量。

sentences.en: And there we actually did not see a significant dip.
sentences.zh: 在那里，我们实际上并没有看到明显的下降。

sentences.en: And so for activities that people identified as productive or discretionary activities that people felt were productive and worthwhile tended to be hobbies.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于人们认为是富有成效的活动，或者人们认为富有成效且有价值的可支配活动，往往是爱好。

sentences.en: So things that are personally enriching, playing sports and exercising.
sentences.zh: 也就是那些能丰富个人生活的事情，比如做运动和锻炼。

sentences.en: So you didn't see a dip there.
sentences.zh: 所以你在那里没有看到下降。

sentences.en: You also did not see a dip.
sentences.zh: 你也没有看到下降。

sentences.en: And actually you saw a sort of linear relationship with socializing.
sentences.zh: 实际上，你看到社交活动呈现出一种线性关系。

sentences.en: So when you're spending your time socially connecting with others, you actually see that there isn't such thing as sort of too much.
sentences.zh: 因此，当你花时间与他人进行社会交往时，你会发现根本不存在所谓“太多”的情况。

sentences.en: It's really the passive leisure that there you see this too much time effect.
sentences.zh: 只有被动休闲才会产生这种时间过多的负面效应。

sentences.en: Huh, interesting.
sentences.zh: 哈，真有趣。

sentences.en: So you spend too much time with your in-laws that there's no such thing than as too much time socializing with people who make you crazy.
sentences.zh: 所以你花太多时间和公公婆婆在一起，那就不存在跟那些让你抓狂的人社交时间过多的说法了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'll leave it to the individual to identify whether it was particularly connecting and worthwhile time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我把这留给个人去判断这是否是特别有连接感和有价值的时间。

sentences.en: But yeah, that gets at the underlying psychology, certainly.
sentences.zh: 不过是的，这确实触及了潜在的心理学原理。

sentences.en: I'm being silly, but I want to talk about a time tracking exercise that you outline in your book.
sentences.zh: 我在开玩笑，但我想谈谈你在书中所概述的一项时间追踪练习。

sentences.en: You recommend people complete this exercise for a couple of weeks, monitor the way that they spend every half hour, the way somebody on a diet might track calories.
sentences.zh: 你建议人们花几周时间完成这项练习，监控他们每半小时的度过方式，就像节食的人记录卡路里那样。

sentences.en: Can you talk a little bit more about that exercise, how you do it and why it's useful?
sentences.zh: 你能多谈谈这个练习吗？你是怎么做的，为什么它很有用？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's useful actually touching back to that two to five hour range, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，它很有用，其实这就呼应了之前提到的两到五个小时的范围，对吧？

sentences.en: Of where it's not about how much time you have available, it's how you spend your time.
sentences.zh: 关键不在于你有多少可用时间，而在于你如何利用时间。

sentences.en: And so then the question is, well, what are the activities that are worthwhile and do produce high levels of happiness and satisfaction?
sentences.zh: 那么问题来了，哪些活动是有价值的，并且确实能带来高水平的幸福感和满意度呢？

sentences.en: Researchers use time tracking data to assess this.
sentences.zh: 研究人员使用时间追踪数据来评估这一点。

sentences.en: So for across individuals looking how, what activities are they doing and how are people feeling while doing those activities?
sentences.zh: 因此，跨越不同人群去观察他们在做什么活动，以及人们在做这些活动时的感受如何。

sentences.en: And from that, you can pull out and look at what are the types of activities that are associated with the most positive emotion?
sentences.zh: 从中，你可以提炼并观察哪些类型的活动与最积极的情绪相关？

sentences.en: What are those activities that tend to be associated with the most negative emotion?
sentences.zh: 哪些活动往往与最消极的情绪相关？

sentences.en: On average, when you're looking across people, you see that the activities that tend to be associated with the most positive emotion are, again, actually social connection.
sentences.zh: 平均而言，当你观察不同人群时，你会发现最容易与最积极情绪相关的活动，依然是社交联系。

sentences.en: So spending quality time with friends and family, also through intimacy.
sentences.zh: 也就是与朋友和家人共度高质量时光，以及通过亲密关系获得的体验。

sentences.en: So socially connecting physically as well.
sentences.zh: 即身体上的社交连接。

sentences.en: The activities that tend to be associated with the least amount of positive emotion, as in the most negative emotion, are quite consistent.
sentences.zh: 往往与最少积极情绪（即最多消极情绪）相关的活动相当一致。

sentences.en: It is commuting, so getting to and from work, hours spent working, so the time you're at work, and housework.
sentences.zh: 那就是通勤（上下班途中）、工作时长（你在工作的时间）以及家务劳动。

sentences.en: But that data is based off of averages.
sentences.zh: 但这些数据是基于平均值的。

sentences.en: So unfortunately for the average American, work is among their least happy hours.
sentences.zh: 因此，对普通美国人来说不幸的是，工作是他们最不快乐的时光之一。

sentences.en: But also it's averaging across category of activities.
sentences.zh: 但这也是对各类活动进行平均的结果。

sentences.en: So it's sort of chunking all of work hours into one category.
sentences.zh: 这就有点像把所有的工作时间都归为一大类。

sentences.en: And I'm sure you can identify, you know, personally, if you're reflecting on your work hours, there are some work activities that are more positive than others.
sentences.zh: 我相信你个人也能感同身受，如果你反思自己的工作时间，会发现有些工作活动比其他活动更积极。

sentences.en: And so this time tracking exercise that I delineate and give sort of clear instructions in the book, as well as a helpful worksheet on my website,
sentences.zh: 因此，我在书中详细阐述并给出了明确指导的这个时间追踪练习，以及我网站上一个有用的工作表，

sentences.en: what it does is it leads you to collect your own personal data.
sentences.zh: 它的作用是引导你收集自己的个人数据。

sentences.en: So over the course of two weeks, and I suggest two weeks more than one week because it's a more sort of complete snapshot of the types of activities that fill your day-to-day life.
sentences.zh: 所以在两周的时间里——我建议两周胜过一周，因为这样能更全面地展现填满你日常生活的活动类型。

sentences.en: But it is how you're spending that time and while you're doing it or as close to completing the activity as possible, rating on a 10-point scale how positive it was.
sentences.zh: 这就是你如何度过这段时间，并在进行时或尽可能在活动完成后，用10分制来评判它的积极程度。

sentences.en: And that includes how enjoyable it was, how satisfying, how meaningful it felt.
sentences.zh: 这包括它有多么令人愉快、有多满足、感觉有多有意义。

sentences.en: So overall positivity.
sentences.zh: 也就是总体上的积极性。

sentences.en: And with this data, your own personalized data, you can at the end of the week.
sentences.zh: 有了这些数据，也就是你自己的个性化数据，你可以在周末得出结论。

sentences.en: And also I would say, suggest that when writing down the particular activity, don't just say work for the reason that I just said.
sentences.zh: 并且我还要建议，在写下特定活动时，不要仅仅写“工作”，原因就是我刚才说的。

sentences.en: Some work hours are going to be more satisfying than others.
sentences.zh: 有些工作时间会比其他时间更令人满意。

sentences.en: So be more specific in the type of work, for instance, or the type of family time that it is.
sentences.zh: 所以要更具体地写明工作的类型，或者家庭时间的类型。

sentences.en: So that you can look back and see what are those activities that for you are associated with the most positive emotion.
sentences.zh: 这样你就可以回顾并找出对你而言哪些活动与最积极的情绪相关。

sentences.en: In addition to identifying those that are most positive and negative activities, you can also see how much time you're spending on these activities.
sentences.zh: 除了识别出最积极和最消极的活动之外，你还可以了解自己在这些活动上花了多少时间。

sentences.en: So you can see, like I teach a course at UCLA to our MBA students called Applying the Science of Happiness to Life Design.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看到，比如我在加州大学洛杉矶分校为工商管理硕士学生开设了一门课程，叫做《将幸福科学应用于生活设计》。

sentences.en: So it's pulling all of the research to share with our students so that they can understand how to spend their time better and feel more fulfilled by it.
sentences.zh: 所以它是把所有的研究提取出来与学生分享，以便他们能理解如何更好地度过时间，并从中感受到更多成就感。

sentences.en: I have them do this exercise and a common observation among students is that they are spending way more time than they expected on social media.
sentences.zh: 我让他们做这个练习，学生中普遍的一个观察是，他们花在社交媒体上的时间远超预期。

sentences.en: And it's not as surprising to us listening to it, but it's always surprising to them because like with this idea that is like, oh, I'll just spend a few minutes here,
sentences.zh: 作为旁听者，我们觉得这并不怎么让人意外，但对他们自己来说总是很惊讶，因为他们的想法就像是，哦，我只在这里花几分钟，

sentences.en: a few minutes there to check.
sentences.zh: 在那儿花几分钟刷一刷。

sentences.en: But those minutes add up to hours.
sentences.zh: 但那些几分钟累积起来就成了几个小时。

sentences.en: And if they look, when they look at their ratings of how positive that time is, it's not very positive.
sentences.zh: 而且如果他们查看，当他们查看自己对这段时间的积极程度评分时，其实并不怎么积极。

sentences.en: It's like a mediocre five.
sentences.zh: 就像是一个平庸的五分。

sentences.en: And these are busy individuals.
sentences.zh: 而且这些人都是大忙人。

sentences.en: They're getting their MBA.
sentences.zh: 他们正在攻读工商管理硕士。

sentences.en: Many of them are working full time as well, have families, and they are time poor.
sentences.zh: 他们许多人还要全职工作，有家庭，而且他们时间极度匮乏。

sentences.en: They're like, oh, my gosh, I don't have enough time to do the things that I really want.
sentences.zh: 他们会觉得，哦，天哪，我没有足够的时间去做我真正想做的事情。

sentences.en: And like those activities in their week, they get the 10, like having dinner with their sister.
sentences.zh: 就像他们一周内的那些活动，能得10分的，比如和姐姐共进晚餐。

sentences.en: They're like, I don't have time to have dinner with my sister.
sentences.zh: 他们会觉得，我没时间跟姐姐吃晚饭。

sentences.en: I'm so busy.
sentences.zh: 我太忙了。

sentences.en: But then when you see that they're spending 15 hours on social media, it's like, oh, actually, this is really informative.
sentences.zh: 但随后当你发现他们在社交媒体上花了15个小时，就会觉得，哦，事实上，这真的很有启发性。

sentences.en: So they can sort of reallocate those hours from activities that are not necessary and that are mediocre in terms of how they contribute to one's happiness and reallocate to those activities that are truly joyful.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们可以把那些不必要且在促进幸福感方面表现平平的活动所花费的时间重新分配，投入到那些真正快乐的活动中去。

sentences.en: So another piece of advice in your book is about the ways in which time is a finite resource and that everything in life ends.
sentences.zh: 所以你书中的另一个建议是关于时间是一种有限的资源，以及生命中的一切终将结束。

sentences.en: And in fact, you suggest something called time left, that you have a time left exercise where you count the number of times you have left of something that you value,
sentences.zh: 事实上，你提出了一个叫做“剩余时间”的概念，你有一个剩余时间练习，让你去数一数你所珍视的东西还剩下多少次，

sentences.en: like how many weekends before your kindergartner goes to college or how many more walks will you get in with your aging dog?
sentences.zh: 比如在你的幼儿园孩子上大学之前还有多少个周末，或者你还能跟正在变老的狗狗散多少次步？

sentences.en: And this seems like it could be an exercise that might make you sad.
sentences.zh: 这看起来可能是一个会让人伤感的练习。

sentences.en: But why is focusing on limited time a route to happiness?
sentences.zh: 但为什么关注有限的时间反而是通往幸福的途径呢？

sentences.en: I'm so glad that you asked it.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你问了这个问题。

sentences.en: And this is a very important and impactful exercise, even though at the face of it, it might seem sad.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常重要且影响深远的练习，尽管表面上看它似乎有些伤感。

sentences.en: The effect that it has on how we spend our time, both the activities that we spend our time on and even our mindset during that time to make the most of it is really critical.
sentences.zh: 它对我们如何度过时间的影响——包括我们把时间花在哪些活动上，甚至包括我们在那段时光中的心态，以充分利用好它——真的至关重要。

sentences.en: In the time tracking, or you can even for yourself reflect back on the last two weeks, what were those moments where you felt true joy?
sentences.zh: 在时间追踪中，或者你自己回顾过去的两周，那些让你感受到真正快乐的时刻是什么？

sentences.en: And even for those of us who are extremely busy, there are likely to be those little snippets in the day that were truly joyful.
sentences.zh: 即使对于我们这些极其忙碌的人来说，一天当中也很有可能会有一些真正快乐的微小片段。

sentences.en: Interestingly, those tend to be very mundane, everyday moments.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，这些往往是非常世俗的日常生活时刻。

sentences.en: And because they're such everyday moments, we tend to assume they will continue happening every day.
sentences.zh: 正因为它们是如此日常的时刻，我们往往会认为它们会每天继续发生。

sentences.en: But what the time's left exercise does is it makes you realize that, in fact, it doesn't.
sentences.zh: 但“剩余时间”练习所做的是，它让你意识到，事实并非如此。

sentences.en: And it actually pulls in a lot of my other research where I find that when people recognize that their time is limited, it makes them savor the time more.
sentences.zh: 它实际上借鉴了我很多其他的研究，我发现当人们认识到自己的时间是有限的时，会让他们更懂得细细品味时间。

sentences.en: So actually,
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，

sentences.en: we find that older people tend to feel greater enjoyment and happiness from ordinary moments than younger people because of their recognition that their time is finite.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，由于意识到自己的时间是有限的，老年人往往比年轻人从平凡的时刻中感受到更多的乐趣和幸福。

sentences.en: But to walk through this exercise in terms of the value of it.
sentences.zh: 但为了从其价值的角度来走一遍这个练习。

sentences.en: So using myself as an example, I will use, I have a six-year-old whom we have this wonderful tradition, which actually started as sort of a routine, part of our morning routine,
sentences.zh: 那么以我自己为例，我有一个六岁的孩子，我们有一个美好的传统，其实它一开始算是一种常规，是我们晨间日常的一部分，

sentences.en: where we would stop after dropping off her big brother in carpool.
sentences.zh: 也就是在拼车送大儿子去学校后我们会停下来。

sentences.en: We would stop at the coffee shop on my way into the office and dropping her off at preschool to get a cup of coffee for me, not her.
sentences.zh: 在我去办公室的路上以及送她去幼儿园的路上，我们会顺便在咖啡店停一下，给我买杯咖啡，不是给她买。

sentences.en: And we would get her a hot chocolate.
sentences.zh: 我们会给她买一杯热巧克力。

sentences.en: And what turned into a caffeine fix, you know, stop for me turned into this wonderful thing each week that we spent this half hour together, just the two of us.
sentences.zh: 而原本变成咖啡因修复的、你知道的为我而设的停留，变成了一件每周都很美好的事情，我们单独共度这半小时，只有我们俩。

sentences.en: And it turned into this beautiful thing that we would anticipate and enjoy and sort of reflect back on.
sentences.zh: 它变成了一件美好的事情，我们会去期盼、享受并回味它。

sentences.en: She's six, so you would think that I would have like a whole lifetime of coffee dates with my daughter.
sentences.zh: 她才六岁，所以你可能会认为我女儿和我会有整整一生一起喝咖啡的约会。

sentences.en: But in actually going through this exercise, which the first step is to calculate how many, so pick something that you enjoy doing.
sentences.zh: 但在真正进行这项练习时，第一步是计算有多少次，所以选一件你喜欢做的事。

sentences.en: Calculate how many times you've done it in your life so far.
sentences.zh: 计算到目前为止你已经在生活中做过多少次了。

sentences.en: Calculate how many times you anticipate being able to do it in your future, accounting for the fact that, well, time, our lives are finite.
sentences.zh: 考虑到时间、我们的生命是有限的这一事实，计算你预计未来还能做多少次。

sentences.en: But sort of even more pressing is that the way that you engage in that activity and the sort of availability of activity is going to shift.
sentences.zh: 但更迫切的是，你参与该活动的方式以及该活动的可用性将会发生转变。

sentences.en: So she's six now, but even before she goes off to college, she's not going to want to, sadly, spend as much time with me.
sentences.zh: 所以她现在六岁，但在她去上大学之前，令人难过的是，她也不会愿意花那么多时间陪我了。

sentences.en: She'll want to, you know, go to the coffee shop with her friends.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她会想和她的朋友们去咖啡店。

sentences.en: So accounting for that, and then she will likely go off to college if she's anything like me.
sentences.zh: 所以考虑到这一点，如果她有点像我的话，她很可能会去上大学。

sentences.en: She'll move from Southern California and, you know, go to school in New York and have her early career in New York.
sentences.zh: 她会离开南加州，你知道的，去纽约上学，并在纽约开启她的早期职业生涯。

sentences.en: So, you know, I'm lucky if I get to visit her and, you know, we have, say, even 10 more coffee dates a year.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，如果我能去探望她，比方说我们每年甚至还有10次咖啡约会，那我就很幸运了。

sentences.en: I calculated, even though she's six, that I have only 36% of our total coffee dates together left.
sentences.zh: 我计算过，尽管她才六岁，但我俩一起的咖啡总约会次数只剩下36%了。

sentences.en: Now, what's the effect of that?
sentences.zh: 现在，这有什么影响呢？

sentences.en: A, at the sort of face of it, you're like, oh, that's sad.
sentences.zh: A，从表面来看，你会觉得，哦，这太让人伤感了。

sentences.en: Yes, it does make me sad, but it's actually really motivating, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，这确实让我伤感，但它实际上真的很具动力，对吧？

sentences.en: Because it makes me darn sure that I am going to carve out, I am not going to schedule meetings so that I'm rushing and that I cancel this time with my daughter.
sentences.zh: 因为它让我绝对确信，我要挤出时间，我绝不会安排会议导致自己时间仓促并取消这段和女儿共度的时光。

sentences.en: When I'm spending that time, I am for sure going to put my phone away and not be distracted during this precious time.
sentences.zh: 当我花这段时间时，我一定会把手机收起来，在这段宝贵的时光里不被分心。

sentences.en: I'm not going to be cycling in my head about all those other things that I have to do.
sentences.zh: 我不会在脑海里反复琢磨所有那些我必须去做的事情。

sentences.en: Because this 30 minutes, that coffee date, that time with my daughter is so precious, it makes me fully engaged.
sentences.zh: 因为这30分钟、那场咖啡约会、这段和我女儿在一起的时光是如此珍贵，它让我全身心地投入。

sentences.en: And it makes her fully engaged.
sentences.zh: 这也让她全身心地投入。

sentences.en: So this is actually another nice point to show that it's not about quantity.
sentences.zh: 所以这其实是另一个很好的观点，表明这无关数量。

sentences.en: This is only 30 minutes that happens each week.
sentences.zh: 这每周只有30分钟。

sentences.en: It is absolutely about quality and how we're spending it, not just the activity, but our mindset during it.
sentences.zh: 它绝对关乎质量以及我们如何度过它，不仅是活动本身，还有我们在其中的心态。

sentences.en: So it leads us to carve out, make the time.
sentences.zh: 所以它引导我们腾出时间，创造时间。

sentences.en: It makes us pay more attention during that time so that that time is higher quality.
sentences.zh: 它让我们在那段时间里付出更多的注意力，从而使那段时间的质量更高。

sentences.en: And then by sort of turning into something special,
sentences.zh: 然后通过将其变成特别的事情，

sentences.en: it allows us to continue to revisit those times in our minds so that those minutes have a significant effect on our overall mood throughout the week.
sentences.zh: 它让我们能够在脑海中不断重温那些时光，从而使这些分钟对我们一整周的整体情绪产生重大影响。

sentences.en: Such that, I mean, the way, the reason I'm so focused on time as the resource that's critical to our happiness is because how we spend our hours sum up to our years,
sentences.zh: 也就是说，我的意思是，我之所以如此关注时间作为对我们的幸福至关重要的资源，是因为我们度过的小时数总和构成了我们的年份，

sentences.en: those years sum up to decades in our life overall.
sentences.zh: 这些年份总和构成了我们一生中的几十年。

sentences.en: And yes, it's the substance of how we're spending the time, but it's also the stories that we're telling, how we think about that time that influences our happiness.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是我们度过时间的实质内容，但也是我们讲述的故事、我们如何看待这段时间，这些都影响着我们的幸福。

sentences.en: With happiness being how you're feeling in the day-to-day and in the moment, as well as a more broader evaluation of how satisfied you feel with your life overall.
sentences.zh: 幸福既包括你在日常和当下的感受，也包括对你整体生活满意度的更广泛评估。

sentences.en: Well, let's talk for a minute about the value of time that, you know, you've been alluding to.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们花一分钟谈谈时间的价值，你知道的，你一直在暗示这个。

sentences.en: You work in a business school and you study how people think about the value of time versus the value of money.
sentences.zh: 你在商学院工作，你研究人们如何看待时间的价值与金钱的价值。

sentences.en: Do most people value time or money more?
sentences.zh: 大多数人更看重时间还是金钱？

sentences.en: And is placing more value on one or the other more likely or less likely to make you happy?
sentences.zh: 把更多的价值放在其中一个上面，是更有可能还是更不可能让你感到幸福？

sentences.en: I am a professor at a business school.
sentences.zh: 我是商学院的一名教授。

sentences.en: Now I got my PhD within a business school.
sentences.zh: 现在我的博士学位也是在商学院获得的。

sentences.en: And even at that time when I was a grad student where I had no money and I didn't have very much time at all,
sentences.zh: 甚至在当年我还是个研究生、没钱又几乎没什么时间的时候，

sentences.en: I was struck that in this context of being surrounded by MBAs and a school that was about sort of helping businesses be successful, that it was solely focused on money.
sentences.zh: 我感到震惊的是，在被工商管理硕士包围的这个环境中，在一所旨在帮助企业取得成功的学校里，它竟然完全专注于金钱。

sentences.en: That money was the way that you assessed success, both individually and for a business.
sentences.zh: 金钱是你评估个人和企业成功的方式。

sentences.en: And that struck me as sort of not true because I was realizing that when I misspent time, I felt much more regretful than when I sort of misspent money.
sentences.zh: 这让我觉得有点不对劲，因为我意识到当我把时间花错地方时，我感到的懊悔远胜于把钱花错地方的时候。

sentences.en: How I was spending my time when it was in ways that felt worthwhile was much more satisfying
sentences.zh: 当我把时间花在那些感觉有意义的事情上时，要满足得多，

sentences.en: and I think much more reflective of me as an individual or I would even say for businesses
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这更能反映我作为一个个体的特点，或者我甚至可以说对于企业而言，

sentences.en: when they are sort of investing in their pursuits in line with what matters to them based off of their mission and values,
sentences.zh: 当他们根据自身的使命和价值观，将其对追求的投资与对他们重要的事情保持一致时，

sentences.en: then that's much more impressive and compelling than sort of solely being profit driven.
sentences.zh: 那么这比单纯由利润驱动要令人印象深刻和引人注目得多。

sentences.en: So I wanted to test this and I did.
sentences.zh: 所以我想要测试这一点，我也确实做了。

sentences.en: Initially, I tested it in the marketing context of leading consumers to think about the time they spent on products versus the money they spent on products.
sentences.zh: 最初，我在引导消费者思考他们在产品上花费的时间与在产品上花费的金钱的营销背景下进行了测试。

sentences.en: And what we found was that thinking about their time invested led people to feel more connected to the product and made them like the product more, like the brand more,
sentences.zh: 我们发现的是，思考他们投入的时间会引导人们对产品感到更有连结，并让他们更喜欢这个产品、更喜欢这个品牌，

sentences.en: because temporal investments are much more personally reflective than our financial ones.
sentences.zh: 因为时间的投入比财务投入更能反映个人个性。

sentences.en: But then I was more interested in not just happiness or satisfaction with one's products, one's buys,
sentences.zh: 但随后我更感兴趣的不仅是对产品、对购买的幸福感或满意度，

sentences.en: but also satisfaction with their choices more broadly and their happiness more generally.
sentences.zh: 还有对他们更广泛选择的满意度以及更普遍的幸福感。

sentences.en: And in that work, what I did was I led people to focus on time versus money
sentences.zh: 在那项工作中，我所做的是引导人们关注时间与金钱，

sentences.en: and then measured how they actually intended to spend their time as well as actually did spend their time.
sentences.zh: 然后衡量他们实际打算如何度过时间以及实际是如何度过时间的。

sentences.en: And what I found was that those who were led to focus on time invested or spent their time
sentences.zh: 我发现，那些被引导去关注所投入或花费时间的人，

sentences.en: in ways that were more fulfilling and felt more worthwhile, more in line with their values.
sentences.zh: 其度过时间的方式更加充实，更有意义，也更符合他们的价值观。

sentences.en: For the most part, that was picking up on, again, spending time in socially connecting ways.
sentences.zh: 在大多数情况下，这再次体现为花时间进行社交连结。

sentences.en: And as a consequence, people felt happier.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们感到了更多的幸福。

sentences.en: More sort of broadly reflective, that was me leading them to think about time or money and seeing the effects.
sentences.zh: 更广泛地反映来看，那是我引导他们思考时间或金钱并观察其效果。

sentences.en: But another work with Hal Hirschfeld, again, we asked people, we asked them a very simple question.
sentences.zh: 但与哈尔·赫施菲尔德的另一项合作中，我们再次询问人们，问了他们一个非常简单的问题。

sentences.en: So hundreds of individuals across the U.S., which do you want more of?
sentences.zh: 全美数百名个体，你们更想要哪一个？

sentences.en: Do you want more time or do you want more money?
sentences.zh: 你们想要更多的时间还是想要更多的钱？

sentences.en: And we found that in that sample, the majority of people said that they would prefer to have more money than more time.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，在该样本中，大多数人表示他们宁愿拥有更多的钱，而不是更多的时间。

sentences.en: In addition to asking them which they would prefer to have more of, we also measured their happiness.
sentences.zh: 除了询问他们更愿意拥有哪一个之外，我们还衡量了他们的幸福感。

sentences.en: So how happy they are in their day-to-day, as well as how satisfied they feel with their lives overall.
sentences.zh: 也就是他们在日常生活中的幸福程度，以及他们对整体生活的满意程度。

sentences.en: And what we found was controlling for the actual amount of money they had, so their income level,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，在控制了他们实际拥有的金钱数量（即收入水平），

sentences.en: controlling for the actual amount of time that they had, which we operationalized by how many hours they work per week, we saw that those who chose having more time were happier.
sentences.zh: 以及控制了他们实际拥有的时间数量（我们通过他们每周工作多少小时来进行操作化定义）之后，我们看到那些选择拥有更多时间的人更幸福。

sentences.en: And that is picking up on the extent to which they value their time as their sort of more precious resource.
sentences.zh: 这反映了他们将时间视为其更珍贵资源的程度。

sentences.en: So that is to say that, yes, the evidence does suggest that being focused on time as the resource that is most precious,
sentences.zh: 也就是说，是的，证据确实表明，专注于将时间作为最珍贵、

sentences.en: as most critical, does lead to greater happiness, does lead to greater satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 最关键的资源，确实能带来更大的幸福感，确实能带来更大的满意度。

sentences.en: And it is because it motivates us to spend in ways that are worthwhile, that do matter,
sentences.zh: 这是因为它激励我们以有价值的、真正重要的方式去度过，

sentences.en: that are intrinsically rewarding and satisfying, such that the outcome, particularly when you are successful, is very fulfilling.
sentences.zh: 以那些具有内在回报和满足感的方式去度过，以至于其结果（特别是当你成功时）是非常充实的。

sentences.en: But also when you are not reaching those goals, it becomes more motivating, as opposed to the sort of general notion of, you know, what I should be doing.
sentences.zh: 但同样，当你没有达到这些目标时，它会变得更具激励性，而不是那种“我应该做什么”的普遍观念。

sentences.en: So oftentimes, you know, particularly teaching MBAs, they come into my class thinking that success in life is money.
sentences.zh: 所以很多时候，特别是教授工商管理硕士时，他们来到我的课堂，认为生活中的成功就是金钱。

sentences.en: How, if only I made a bunch more money, then I would be happier.
sentences.zh: 如果我能赚更多更多的钱，那么我就会更幸福。

sentences.en: The problem with that is that a bunch more money, there's always someone that's making more.
sentences.zh: 这其中的问题在于，赚更多更多的钱，总会有人赚得更多。

sentences.en: And oftentimes, we assess how we're doing by looking at how we're doing compared to those around us.
sentences.zh: 而且很多时候，我们通过观察自己与周围人的比较来评估我们的表现。

sentences.en: So this is social comparison.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是社会比较。

sentences.en: And a sort of unfortunate piece of this is that when you make more money, the folks around you tend to also be making a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 其中一个不幸的部分是，当你赚更多钱时，你周围的人往往也会赚很多钱。

sentences.en: So once you, you know, make more money and move into a nicer neighborhood, then there's neighbors that are also making more money.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦你赚了更多钱并搬到一个更好的社区，就会有邻居也赚更多的钱。

sentences.en: And there's always someone that's going to make more.
sentences.zh: 总会有人赚得更多。

sentences.en: When you use time as your sort of metric, and again, because it is more reflective of your intrinsic values,
sentences.zh: 当你把时间作为你的衡量标准时，而且再次因为时间更能反映你的内在价值观，

sentences.en: then you're not subject to the social comparison.
sentences.zh: 那么你就不会受制于社会比较。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Everybody has 24 hours in a day.
sentences.zh: 每个人一天都有24小时。

sentences.en: They can't have 48 and you have 24.
sentences.zh: 他们不可能有48小时而你只有24小时。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So using your own sort of values, what matters as your gauge and motivator compared to these general notions of what success is, which in our culture tends to be money.
sentences.zh: 所以将你自己的价值观、什么才是重要的事情作为你的衡量标准和激励源，而不是那些关于成功是什么的普遍观念（在我们的文化中往往是金钱）。

sentences.en: Well, so speaking of value, you published a paper a few years ago that found that when people give their time away,
sentences.zh: 好吧，说到价值，你几年前发表了一篇论文，发现当人们付出时间时，

sentences.en: so when they spend their time helping other people, they feel like they have more time.
sentences.zh: 也就是当他们花时间帮助别人时，他们会觉得自己有更多的时间。

sentences.en: And that seems kind of counterintuitive.
sentences.zh: 这似乎有点违反直觉。

sentences.en: How did you come to that conclusion?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么得出这个结论的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I'm so glad you asked about that because it sort of touches on one of the things that I said at the beginning was when we feel time poor,
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你问到这个，因为它触及了我一开始说的一点，那就是当我们感到时间匮乏时，

sentences.en: we become less kind because we are busy and we're like, oh, my gosh, I don't have enough time for anything, let alone to slow down and spend time to help someone else.
sentences.zh: 我们就会变得不再那么善良，因为我们很忙，会想：哦，天哪，我连任何事情的时间都不够，更不用说慢下来花时间去帮助别人了。

sentences.en: But what we found in this work, we conducted it on a Saturday among adults and in the morning we gave them a set of instructions.
sentences.zh: 但我们在研究中发现，我们在一个周六对成年人进行了这项研究，在早晨我们给他们提供了一组指令。

sentences.en: Half of the participants whom we randomly assigned, we told them spend 30 minutes today doing something for someone else that you weren't already planning to do.
sentences.zh: 我们随机分配了一半的参与者，告诉他们今天花30分钟为别人做一件你本来没打算做的事。

sentences.en: We told the other participants, spend 30 minutes today doing something for yourself that you weren't already planning to do.
sentences.zh: 我们告诉另一组参与者，今天花30分钟为自己做一件你本来没打算做的事。

sentences.en: And then that evening, we followed up with them, asked how they spent that time, but more importantly, how much time they felt like they had, how time affluent they were.
sentences.zh: 然后在那天晚上，我们对他们进行了回访，询问他们是如何度过这段时间的，但更重要的是，他们觉得自己有多少时间，他们有多么充裕的时间。

sentences.en: And I love doing this study because people did nice things both for themselves and others.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢做这项研究，因为人们既为自己也为别人做了美好的事情。

sentences.en: So it's like the types of things that they did for other people, some was for people, someone that they knew well,
sentences.zh: 所以就像他们为别人做的那类事情，有些是为人们做的，为他们非常熟悉的人，

sentences.en: like making a nice meal for their partner, helping a friend pull up a tile in the bathroom for some reason that went out, was stuck out, writing a letter to one's grandmother.
sentences.zh: 比如为伴侣做一顿美味的饭菜，帮朋友把浴室里由于某种原因突出来、卡住的瓷砖撬起来，给祖母写一封信。

sentences.en: Others did something not for someone they knew, but more generally kind to their community.
sentences.zh: 其他人做的不是为了他们认识的人，而是对他们的社区更加普遍地表现出善良。

sentences.en: So going to the park, picking up trash.
sentences.zh: 比如去公园捡垃圾。

sentences.en: The types of things that people did for themselves were sort of pampering, going for a run, reading a book.
sentences.zh: 人们为自己做的事情有点像纵容自己、去跑步、读一本书。

sentences.en: What we found was that irrespective of the particular way they gave time, those who spent time on someone else reported that they had more time.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，无论他们付出时间的具体方式如何，那些把时间花在别人身上的人报告说他们有更多的时间。

sentences.en: And the question is why?
sentences.zh: 问题是为什么？

sentences.en: And what our data follow-up studies suggested is that when we spend time to help others, it makes us feel very accomplished.
sentences.zh: 我们的数据和后续研究表明，当我们花时间去帮助别人时，这让我们感到非常有成就感。

sentences.en: The sense of greater self-efficacy.
sentences.zh: 这种更高的自我效能感。

sentences.en: And so you're like, I accomplished a lot.
sentences.zh: 所以你会觉得：我完成了好多事情。

sentences.en: And if you recall, the definition of time poverty is the feeling of having too much to do and not enough time to do it.
sentences.zh: 如果你还记得的话，时间贫困的定义就是觉得自己有太多事情要做却没有足够的时间去完成。

sentences.en: So basically having the temporal resources to satisfy the goals of all the things that you want to do.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是拥有满足你想做的所有事情的目标所需的时间资源。

sentences.en: So when you realize how much you can accomplish with your time, it makes that time that you have feel more expansive.
sentences.zh: 所以当你意识到你可以用你的时间完成多少事情时，会让你拥有的时间感觉更加充裕。

sentences.en: You're like, oh, actually, I can accomplish what I want to and set out to do versus spending time on oneself, which doesn't increase a sense of self-efficacy.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得，哦，实际上，我可以完成我想做和着手去做的事情，而不是把时间花在自己身上，这并不能增加自我效能感。

sentences.en: We also had studies comparing it to an even more stringent comparison.
sentences.zh: 我们还进行了将它与更严格的对照组进行比较的研究。

sentences.en: So not spending time on oneself, but actually getting a windfall of free time.
sentences.zh: 所以不是把时间花在自己身上，而是真正获得了一笔意外的空闲时间。

sentences.en: So in this study, it was among undergraduate students who were participating in a lab study.
sentences.zh: 所以在这次研究中，对象是参与实验室研究的本科生。

sentences.en: And at the end of the study, we told half of them, please spend this 15 minutes helping a high school student by editing a college application essay.
sentences.zh: 在研究结束时，我们告诉其中一半的人，请花这15分钟通过修改大学申请短文来帮助一名高中生。

sentences.en: We told the others, actually, you know, all the essays have been edited.
sentences.zh: 我们告诉其他人，事实上，你知道的，所有的短文都已经被修改好了。

sentences.en: You have 15 minutes.
sentences.zh: 你们有15分钟时间。

sentences.en: You have a windfall of 15 minutes of free time in your day.
sentences.zh: 你们在这一天里意外获得了15分钟的空闲时间。

sentences.en: We measured for everyone how much time did they feel like they had.
sentences.zh: 我们测量了每个人感觉自己有多少时间。

sentences.en: Those who had spent the time helping the high school student edit the essay felt like they had more time compared to those who had that 15-minute windfall.
sentences.zh: 那些花时间帮助高中生修改短文的人，与那些只是意外获得了15分钟空闲时间的人相比，觉得自己的时间更多了。

sentences.en: That is why even though when we feel time poor and we don't feel like we have minutes to spare to help others,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么尽管当我们感到时间匮乏、觉得没有多余的分钟去帮助别人时，

sentences.en: actually taking the time, spending the time to help someone will make you feel like you have more time.
sentences.zh: 实际上抽出时间、花时间去帮助别人会让你觉得自己的时间更多。

sentences.en: Now, I will say there is such thing as giving too much time.
sentences.zh: 现在，我要说的是，付出太多时间也是存在的。

sentences.en: And so if you're giving so much of your time that you're not truly able to take care of the needs and what you need to accomplish in your day, then you actually see a backlash.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你付出了如此多的时间，以至于你无法真正照顾好自己的需求以及你在一天中需要完成的事情，那么你实际上会看到反弹效应。

sentences.en: And also, if it feels like people are taking your time as opposed to you giving your time, then you don't see this positive effect.
sentences.zh: 而且，如果感觉人们是在夺走你的时间，而不是你在奉献时间，那么你就看不到这种积极的效果。

sentences.en: So there's not our research, but in the whole field of research of caregivers, it can be very depleting.
sentences.zh: 因此，这不是在我们的研究中，而是在整个照顾者的研究领域中，这可能会非常消耗精力。

sentences.en: So long-term caregiving, that it does feel like an obligation.
sentences.zh: 因此，长期的照顾，确实让人感觉像是一种义务。

sentences.en: So it's not you giving it.
sentences.zh: 所以这不是你主动付出的。

sentences.en: It's being sort of absorbed there.
sentences.zh: 它更像是被那种氛围所吞噬了。

sentences.en: You don't see the sort of positive boost in time affluence.
sentences.zh: 你不会看到时间充裕度方面的这种积极提升。

sentences.en: So here's a question for those of us who spend our weekends cleaning the house and running errands.
sentences.zh: 所以，对于我们这些周末打扫房子和跑腿办事的人来说，这里有个问题。

sentences.en: Are there ways to make these necessary, very time-intensive chores feel less onerous?
sentences.zh: 有没有什么方法能让这些必要的、非常耗时的杂务感觉不那么繁重？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 有的。

sentences.en: And there's two different answers for that.
sentences.zh: 对此有两个不同的答案。

sentences.en: First is, regardless of whether it happens on the weekend, as I mentioned, activities, household chores are among our least happy.
sentences.zh: 首先，不管它是否发生在周末，正如我所提到的，各项活动、家务活是我们最不快乐的事情之一。

sentences.en: There is a bundling strategy that you can do to make that time that you spend on chores more fulfilling.
sentences.zh: 有一种捆绑策略你可以用来让你花在做家务上的时间更有意义。

sentences.en: You can also use this for commuting.
sentences.zh: 你也可以把这个方法用在通勤上。

sentences.en: So if you bundle this unfun activity, I would say, with an activity that you do like to do and you want to do, then those hours are going to feel more enjoyable.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你把这个不好玩的活动——我想这么说——与一个你喜欢做且想做的活动结合起来，那么那些小时就会感觉更加愉快。

sentences.en: So as an example, while unloading the dishwasher and doing the laundry, if you actually bundle that time of spending doing chores,
sentences.zh: 举个例子，在卸洗碗机和洗衣服的同时，如果你把做家务的时间进行捆绑，

sentences.en: listening to podcasts where you get to enrich your sort of knowledge, particularly speaking of psychology,
sentences.zh: 去听那些能丰富你的知识、特别是说到心理学方面的播客，

sentences.en: or listening to an audiobook, then, and I will also say that in our data, we find that one of the top things that people don't do
sentences.zh: 或者听有声书，那么——我也要说，在我们的数据中，我们发现人们不做的事情中排名前几的一项是

sentences.en: because they don't feel like they have enough time is reading for pleasure.
sentences.zh: 因为他们觉得自己没有足够的时间去进行纯粹的阅读。

sentences.en: But if you actually bundle this time that you're spending on chores with increasing your perspective and interests through audiobooks or reading,
sentences.zh: 但如果你把花在做家务上的时间与通过有声书或阅读来开拓视野和兴趣结合起来，

sentences.en: then that time itself becomes more fulfilling.
sentences.zh: 那么这段时间本身就会变得更有意义。

sentences.en: There's another intervention that I love with Colin West and Sanford DeVoe where we found that simply treating your weekend like a vacation
sentences.zh: 还有另一个我非常喜欢的由科林·韦斯特和桑福德·德沃开展的干预研究，我们发现仅仅把你的周末当作假期来对待

sentences.en: makes you happier when you return to work on Monday, and it makes you enjoy the weekend more.
sentences.zh: 会让你在周一返回工作岗位时更快乐，并且会让你更享受周末。

sentences.en: The reason that this happens is because weekends are breaks.
sentences.zh: 之所以会这样，是因为周末就是休息。

sentences.en: So I will also say that we as Americans are really bad at taking breaks.
sentences.zh: 所以我也要说，我们美国人真的很不擅长休息。

sentences.en: We don't take vacation.
sentences.zh: 我们不度假。

sentences.en: We are one of the few industrialized countries that doesn't have legally mandated paid vacation.
sentences.zh: 我们是极少数没有法定带薪休假的发达国家之一。

sentences.en: Even though we get less vacation, we don't take it.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们的假期很少，但我们还是不休假。

sentences.en: About half of Americans don't take all of their paid vacation.
sentences.zh: 大约有一半的美国人没有休完他们所有的带薪假期。

sentences.en: So we don't take vacation because we don't feel like we have time and we don't have money.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不度假，是因为我们觉得我们没有时间，也没有钱。

sentences.en: But taking breaks, taking vacation is important because it's associated with greater creativity.
sentences.zh: 但休息、度假是很重要的，因为它与更高的创造力息息相关。

sentences.en: It actually makes you more engaged in your work and it makes you happier.
sentences.zh: 它实际上会让你更投入到工作中，并让你更快乐。

sentences.en: So take vacation, period.
sentences.zh: 所以，去度假吧，就这么简单。

sentences.en: But also we have breaks in the regular cadence of our weeks.
sentences.zh: 但我们每周的固定节奏中也有休息时间。

sentences.en: Every week we have two days off and most working Americans do get the weekends off.
sentences.zh: 我们每周有两天假，大多数上班的美国人确实享有周末假期。

sentences.en: But why does it not feel like a break?
sentences.zh: 但为什么它感觉不像是在休息？

sentences.en: It's because it's part of our routine.
sentences.zh: 这是因为它已经成了我们日常常规的一部分。

sentences.en: We're not paying attention.
sentences.zh: 我们没有集中注意力。

sentences.en: We're sort of rushing through all of our to-dos, rushing through our activities to get to, you know, check off items on our to-do liSt.
sentences.zh: 我们只是在匆忙完成所有的待办事项，匆忙完成各项活动，为了去，你知道的，勾掉待办事项列表上的项目。

sentences.en: But when you treat it like a vacation, and so we ran several experiments replicating this effect, which I love.
sentences.zh: 但是，当你把它当作假期来对待时——我们做过几次重复这一效果的实验，我非常喜欢。

sentences.en: So it was among working adults going into a weekend on a Friday.
sentences.zh: 所以对象是在周五即将迎来周末的上班族。

sentences.en: We randomly assigned half of them.
sentences.zh: 我们随机将他们分为两组。

sentences.en: We gave them the simple instructions.
sentences.zh: 我们给了他们简单的指令。

sentences.en: Treat this weekend like a vacation.
sentences.zh: 把这个周末当作假期来过。

sentences.en: That is, to the extent possible, think in ways and behave in ways you would on vacation.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，在可能的情况下，以你在度假时的方式去思考和行事。

sentences.en: The others, we said, treat this weekend like a regular weekend.
sentences.zh: 对于其他人，我们说，把这个周末当作一个普通的周末来过。

sentences.en: To the extent possible, think in ways and behave in ways you would on a regular weekend.
sentences.zh: 在可能的情况下，以你在过普通周末时的方式去思考和行事。

sentences.en: That was it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: That was our sort of intervention.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的那种干预措施。

sentences.en: On Monday, when they were back at work, we followed up with them and we measured their happiness.
sentences.zh: 到了周一，当他们回到工作岗位时，我们对他们进行了回访，并测量了他们的幸福感。

sentences.en: And we saw that those who treated the weekend like a vacation ended up happier on Monday.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，那些把周末当作假期来过的人在周一的时候更加快乐。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Well, we looked at how they spent their time over the course of the weekend.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们观察了他们在整个周末是如何度过时间的。

sentences.en: Yes, they did spend a little bit more of their time doing vacation-like things.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们确实花了一点更多的时间去做类似度假的事情。

sentences.en: They stayed in bed a little longer.
sentences.zh: 他们在床上多赖了一会儿。

sentences.en: So for that physical intimacy, they spent more time eating.
sentences.zh: 为了那种身体上的亲密感，他们花了更多时间吃东西。

sentences.en: They spent less time doing housework and less time doing work work.
sentences.zh: 他们花在做家务上的时间更少，花在工作上的时间也更少。

sentences.en: But interestingly, it wasn't the time that they spent on activities that relayed into their enjoyment of the weekend or into their happiness on Monday.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，转化他们周末享受度或周一幸福感的并不是他们在各项活动上花的时间。

sentences.en: What it was was their mindset.
sentences.zh: 起作用的是他们的心态。

sentences.en: Those who treated the weekend like a vacation were more present during their activities.
sentences.zh: 那些把周末当作假期来过的人在活动期间更加专注于当下。

sentences.en: So they were paying more attention to the present moment.
sentences.zh: 所以他们对当前时刻投入了更多的关注。

sentences.en: And it's that paying attention to the present moment made them like their activities more and made them feel more refreshed when they got back to work on Monday.
sentences.zh: 正是这种对当下时刻的关注，让他们更喜欢自己的活动，并在周一重返工作岗位时感到更加神清气爽。

sentences.en: And so it's absolutely a mindset thing that it's not about the sort of routine of getting through things.
sentences.zh: 所以这绝对是一种心态问题，它与应付事情的常规流程无关。

sentences.en: It is about having a break like a vacation such that you can chill out and be in the moment even if you're doing the same thing, even if you're like having, you know, a pancake
sentences.zh: 关键是要像度假一样拥有一个假期，这样你就能放松身心并融入当下，哪怕你做的是同样的事情，哪怕你是在吃，你知道的，煎饼

sentences.en: breakfast or even if you're the one cooking the pancake breakfast for your family on Saturday
sentences.zh: 早餐，或者哪怕是在周六早晨为家人做煎饼早餐的那个人，

sentences.en: morning, when it's like a regular weekend, you're just sort of doing it and getting through it.
sentences.zh: 当它像一个普通周末时，你只是在应付它、完成它。

sentences.en: When it's like a vacation, it feels so much different.
sentences.zh: 当它像一个假期时，感觉就完全不同了。

sentences.en: It feels so different.
sentences.zh: 感觉太不一样了。

sentences.en: And you engage with the people that you're with.
sentences.zh: 并且你会与身边的人进行互动。

sentences.en: So in a very different way.
sentences.zh: 以一种非常不同的方式。

sentences.en: So treat the weekend like a vacation.
sentences.zh: 所以，把周末当作假期来过吧。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Holmes, I hate to say this, but we're out of time.
sentences.zh: 好吧，霍姆斯博士，我不想这么说，但我们的时间到了。

sentences.en: So I want to thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 所以我要感谢你今天能来参加我们的节目。

sentences.en: It's been really interesting and fun to talk to you.
sentences.zh: 和你交谈非常有趣且有意义。

sentences.en: I think you've given us all some good ideas about how we can use our time more productively in a way that will make us happy.
sentences.zh: 我想你给我们所有人都提供了一些很好的建议，关于我们如何能以一种让我们快乐的方式更有效率地利用时间。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Well, thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: It was a treat.
sentences.zh: 这是一次美妙的体验。
